papers.authors: Sabrina Grandclaude, Didier Grandclaude, Thierry Nobre, Cadenza Academic Translations
papers.summary: Based on the analysis of 96 organizational innovation in healthcare (OIH) projects and 52 interviews conducted with project leaders initiating these innovations, this research identifies the phenomena underlying the genesis of OIHs. The results highlight the major role played by factors such as patient empathy, international inspiration, academic inspiration, technological inspiration, serendipitous encounters, and the desire for organizational transformation in driving the generation of OIHs. Furthermore, our findings emphasize the dual nature of the research and development process for these innovations, characterized as both ex nihilo and ex materia.

papers.title: A collaborative and participatory approach to public service innovation: Health sector dynamics and outlook
papers.title_ja: 公衆衛生サービスイノベーションへの協働的かつ参加型アプローチ：保健セクターのダイナミクスと展望
papers.authors: Fatima Yatim, Alan Sitkin, Cadenza Academic Translations
papers.summary: This article explores the dynamics of collaborative and participatory innovations in public health services using Chen et al.’s (2020) typology. Based on a mixed survey of projects awarded under the national “Droits des usagers de la santé” initiative, the study finds that user participation primarily generates operational and capacity-oriented innovations frequently involving external partnerships. The analysis highlights the crucial interactions between internal and external dynamics, identifying essential conditions for successful innovations: effective mobilization of internal resources, robust institutional support, and early and active user involvement. However, the study also identifies limitations in citizen engagement, particularly in the evaluation phase of innovations. The article concludes by suggesting avenues for enhancing full co-creation processes in public services to maximize public value.

papers.title_ja: 感情的萎縮に抵抗する：高等教育における（そして高等教育のための）愛の回復の痛みと喜び
papers.summary: This paper analyses reflections from a collective autoethnography on refusing to reject love in higher education. Extensive research and commentary documents an increasing instrumentalization and commercialisation of universities evident in ‘workload optimisation’, exclusive admissions and insufficient support systems, output-driven performance criteria, restrictive models of research and publication, and the encouragement of shallow pedagogical approaches. This has the un-/intended effect of what we describe as ‘emotional shrinkage’, the suppression of time, space, and inclination, for imagining and realising love for self and others. In this context, gestures of love can be understood as acts of conscious resistance. papers.title: Beyond the Dancefloor: Club Culture, Design and Nightlife
papers.title_ja: ダンスフロアを超えて：クラブ文化、デザイン、ナイトライフ
papers.summary: Beyond the Dance Floor offers the first critical inquiry into the relationship between design, club culture and broader international culture and creativity. Building on the editors’ pioneering work on the design and architecture history of nightclubs in the late 20th and early 21st centuries, this collection of new research will show the significant but under-recognized creativity of club culture and explore how its broader design-based interactions go beyond the dancefloor into the world outside the nightclub. Beyond the Dancefloor will assert the social, cultural, economic, and political, value of club culture by revealing its embeddedness in broader creative and cultural communities, industries and practices. papers.summary_ja: 『ダンスフロアを超えて』はデザイン、クラブ文化、より広範な国際文化・創造性の関係に関する初めての批評的調査を提供する。編集者らによる20世紀後期から21世紀初期のナイトクラブのデザインと建築史に関する先駆的研究を基に展開される。
papers.novelty_reason: ナイトライフとデザイン理論の学際的結合は、都市文化研究に新たな美学的・建築的視点をもたらしている。
